rules.title: Tenant screening fee cap, receipts and refunds (Civil Code 1950.6)
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge a screening fee only up to the annual maximum ($68.96 for 2026) and must give applicants a copy of any credit report, a receipt with itemized costs, and a refund of any unused portion. They cannot charge a fee when no unit is available, and must return fees to applicants not selected unless they use a first-qualified-applicant policy; they must accept a reusable screening report if one is provided.
rules.quoted_span: Prospective tenants should expect to receive a copy of their credit report within 7 days of receipt by the landlord, a receipt for the fee paid and an itemized list of any out-of-pocket expenses and time spent by the landlord on the screening, and a refund of any unused portion of the fee.
rules.coverage_text: Prospective tenants applying to rent residential units
rules.interaction: Berkeley BMC 13.78.010 requires landlords to disclose the state fee cap under Civil Code 1950.6(b) and a tenant screening fee rights statement.
rules.extraction_note: State law summarized on Berkeley Rent Board page; the $68.96 2026 figure appears as a heading fragment rather than a full sentence, so the quoted span covers the receipt/refund requirements. No enactment or effective dates given.

rules.title: Notification of state law limitation on tenant screening fees
rules.requirement: An owner who charges a fee for a credit report or to process an application must provide, in the application or a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap under Civil Code 1950.6(b).
rules.key_value: Required pre-fee disclosure of screening fee rights and state fee cap
rules.quoted_span: When an owner or the owner’s agent gets a request to rent residential property in Berkeley from an applicant and the owner charges a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and to validate, review, or otherwise process an application, the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under
rules.coverage_text: Residential rental property in Berkeley; applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of contrary contractual language (BMC 13.78.018).
rules.interaction: Supplements California Civil Code 1950.6 by requiring disclosure of the state fee cap; does not replace the state rule.
rules.extraction_note: The statement's URL is still to be provided by the City per the page. No adoption or effective date stated. Quoted span ends mid-sentence because the source breaks the sentence with a link to Civil Code 1950.6(b).

rules.title: Prohibition of non-refundable fees associated with existing tenancies
rules.requirement: Owners and their agents cannot charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, including fees tied to a roommate leaving or requests to add or replace a roommate. Contrary lease provisions are unenforceable.
rules.key_value: No non-refundable renewal or roommate fees for existing tenants
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
rules.coverage_text: Existing tenants of residential rental property in Berkeley; applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of contrary lease language (BMC 13.78.018).
rules.interaction: Local rule in addition to state screening fee law.
rules.extraction_note: BMC 13.78.018 makes violating lease provisions unenforceable; no fine or damages stated. No adoption or effective date stated.
